questions.question: If Cosec θ + Cot θ = m, find the value of frac{m²−1}{m²+1}.
questions.solution:
Identity used:

cosec²θ – cot²θ = 1

Calculation:

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = m ---- (1)

⇒ (cosec θ - cot θ)(cosec θ + cot θ) = 1

⇒ (cosec θ - cot θ) =1/m

⇒ cosec θ - cot θ = 1/m ---- (2)

By adding (1) and (2), we'll get

2cosecθ = m + 1/m

cosecθ = (m² + 1)/2m ...(3)

By subtracting (1) and (2), we'll get

2cotθ = m - 1/m ...(4)

cotθ = (m2 - 1)/2m

⇒ frac{m²−1}{m²+1}

Putting eq. (3) annd (4) in above expression:

⇒ 2mcotθ/2mcosecθ 

⇒ cotθ/cosecθ

⇒ cosθ

**The value is cosθ.**

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio (4)/(5):(5)/(6):(9)/(10). The difference between the smallest and the greatest numbers is 12. Find the number which is NEITHER the smallest NOR the greatest.
questions.solution:
Given

Three numbers are in the ratio (4)/(5):(5)/(6):(9)/(10).

Calculation

⇒ 4/5 × 12 = 9.6

⇒ 5/6 × 12 = 10

⇒ 9/10 × 12 = 10.8

The three numbers are in the ratio = 9.6:10:10.8

Let the numbers be 9.6x, 10x, and 10.8x.

⇒ 10.8x - 9.6x = 12

⇒ 1.2x = 12

⇒ x = 10

The numbers are 96, 100 and 108

The number which is NEITHER the smallest NOR the greatest is 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__

Calculation:

LCM of 5, 6 and 10 is 30.

4/5 × 30 = 24

5/6 × 30 = 25

9/10 × 30 = 27

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C = 24x ∶ 25x ∶ 27x

According to the question 

⇒ 27x - 24x = 12

⇒ 3x = 12

⇒ x = 4

First number = 24x = 24 × 4 = 96

Second number = 25x = 25 × 4 = 100

Third number = 27x = 27 × 4 = 108

The correct option is 3 i.e. 100

questions.question: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 15 cm and 13 cm, whose centres are 14 cm apart, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Radii of circles are 13 cm and 15 cm 

Distance between centres = 14 cm 

Concept Used:

The line joining the centers of two circles is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord of the two circles.

⇒ AB = 2AM

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6008f37fd7b12402914c8a9d494de1501df6065c15024a36901891c01373a2bd.png] 

From the figure, P and Q are the centers of two circles of radius 15 cm and 13cm respectively and AB is the common chord

In ΔAMP, PA = 15 cm

By Pythagoras theorem,

AM² = PA² - PM²

⇒ AM2 = 152 - PM2

⇒ AM2 = 225 - PM2 -----(1)

In ΔAMQ, QA = 13 cm

By Pythagoras theorem,

AM2 = QA2 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 132 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 169 - MQ2 -----(2)

From (1) and (2)

225 - PM2 = 169 - MQ2 

⇒ PM2 - MQ2 = 56

⇒ (PM + MQ) (PM - MQ) = 56

According to the question,

(PM + MQ) = PQ = Distance between centres = 14 cm ----(3)

⇒ 14 (PM - MQ) = 56

⇒ (PM - MQ) = 56/14 = 4 ----(4)

From (3) and (4)

PM = 9 cm

Putting value of PM in (1)

AM2 = 225 - 92

⇒ AM2 = 225 - 81

⇒ AM2 = 144

⇒ AM = 12 cm

Thus, length of common chord = AB = 2AM = 24 cm

**∴ The length of the common chord is 24 cm.**

questions.question: A can do a certain piece of work in 1.5 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do the same piece of work in 30 days and C alone can do it in 120 days, then how many days will B take to do this piece of work alone?
questions.solution:
Given:-

A can do a certain piece of work in 1.5 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it.

 A and B together can do the same piece of work in 30 days

C alone can do it in 120 days

Concept:-

The ratio of efficiency is reciprocal of time.

Number of days required to complete a certain work = (Work to be completed/Work efficiency)

Calculation:-

A = 1.5 (B + C)

A/(B + C) = 3/2

A/(B + C)(efficiency) = 2/3

Total work be 120(LCM of 30 and 120)

Efficiency of A + B = 120/30 = 4 unit/day

Efficiency of C = 120/120 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 4 - 2 = 2 unit/day

Time taken by B to do this piece of work alone = 120/2

= 60 days.

**The time taken by B to do this piece of work alone is 60 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1556ee60888002fb4e3099c1b21fe169dc143b61a34f906e29285d84c78222bb.png] 

The time taken by B to do this piece of work alone is 60 days.

questions.question: Aarti can type 85 pages in 10 hours. Aarti and Bina together can type 500 pages in 40 hours. How much time will Bina take to type 40 pages?
questions.solution:
Given:

Aarti can type 85 pages in 10 hours

Aarti and Bina together can type 500 pages in 40 hours

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Work done/Time Taken

Calculation:

By using the above formula

The efficiency of Aarti is = 85/10 = 8.5 pages/hr

The efficiency of Aarti and Bina = 500/40= 12.5 pages/hr

The efficiency of Bina = 12.5 - 8.5 = 4 pages/hr

The time taken by Bina to type 40 pages will be

⇒ 40/4= 10 hr

∴ The Time taken by Bina is 10 hours.

questions.question: Find the least number divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18, which is a perfect square.
questions.solution:
**Concept used**

To find the least perfect square number which is divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18

first, find the LCM of the given numbers

**Calculation**

LCM (2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18) = 90

90 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5.

As 2 and 5 are not in pair in LCM’s factor so we need to multiply 90 by 5 and 2 to make it a perfect square.

90 x 2 x 5 = 900.

**∴ 900 is the least perfect square divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18**

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a piece of work in 6 days. If P can alone complete the work in 18 days, then the number of days required for Q to finish the work is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

P and Q together can complete a piece of work in 6 days.

P can alone complete the work in 18 days.

**Formula used:**

Total work = man × efficiency

**Calculation**

P’s 1-day work = 1/18

(P + Q)’s 1 day work = 1/6

Q’s 1 day work = 1/6 – 1/18 = 1/9

**Hence, Q can alone do the work in 9 days**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** Q’s = [(P + Q) × P] /(P + Q - P)

Q’s = (18 × 6)/(18 - 6)

Q’s = 9 days.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters in the voter list did not cast their vote, whereas 10% of the votes cast were found to be invalid. The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes. What is the total number of voters enrolled in the voter list?
questions.solution:
Given:

10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 10% of the polled vote were found invalid.

The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes.

Concept Used:

The percentage is calculated based on 100 i.e. 100 is the base

40% means 40 out of 100

Calculation:

Let, the total enrolled voters be x

10% did not cast a vote means cast or polled vote = 9x/10

10% vote is invalid

That means valid vote = (90/100) × (9x/10)

⇒ 81x/100

The winning candidate got 56% of the polled vote means the looser got (100 – 56) = 44% vote

Winer candidate got total {(56/100) × (81x/100)} vote

And the looser candidate got {(44/100) × (81x/100)} vote

Accordingly,

{(56/100) × (81x/100)} - {(44/100) × (81x/100)} = 1458

⇒ (81x/100) × {(56 – 44)/100} = 1458

⇒ (81 × 12)x/10000 = 1458

⇒ x = (1458× 10000)/(81 × 12)

⇒ x = 15000

∴ Total 15000 voters enrolled in the voter list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Total voters = 1458 × (100/90) × (100/90) × 100\(56 - 44) = 15000
